content:
Hi, I usually use a variety of languages in my workflow (each one is suited for a different purpose), and separate every language in its file. Every file has a shebang, which lets me run it very easily from Kate with F5 without altering permissions, whether it's bash, Python, ...

I tried to do the same for .lean files (cfr. https://lean-lang.org/functional_programming_in_lean/Hello___-World___/Running-a-Program/#running-a-program), but it doesn't seem to be working out as I have planned, as lean thinks the shebang is part of the code.

Any ideas? I prefer running my programs this way to keep things simple rather than using a complex UI for things :)

#!/home/yalihupokn/.elan/bin/lean
def main : IO Unit := IO.println "Hello, world!"
I think ignoring shebang sounds like a good feature request!

Snir Broshi said:

I think ignoring shebang sounds like a good feature request!

Ok, will give it a try
What version of Lean would you want this to use?

Eric Wieser said:

What version of Lean would you want this to use?

I would say 4, since it's the latest
I think the question here is which 4.x. Lean is still in the phase where there is still much incompatibility between minor versions, which is why this was asked

Weiyi Wang said:

I think the question here is which 4.x. Lean is still in the phase where there is still much incompatibility between minor versions, which is why this was asked

I see, honestly I don't mind. I think I realised Lean isn't really intended for this kind of usage anyway, as @Joachim Breitner suggested. @Snir Broshi the link you see on the previous sentence takes you to the issue I posted in case you're interested, I've explored alternatives to the shebang there.
